label: high-scale transactional factory

packaged_from.digest_purpose: The commit alone names the target; the per-file digests let the fidelity test verify what it materialised from git rather than trust it. Recomputable with `git cat-file blob dd2fcc63694bea365153a5930472816037b6e4ff:workstreams/po03/tools/<file> | sha256sum`.
packaged_from.read_method: read-only; the live modules are never written to and never imported at runtime by the packaged generation

why_a_port_and_not_an_import: control_plane.py binds its ledger, registry, dispatch and recovery paths to module-level constants under workstreams/po03/control/, which is coordinator-owned shared state. Importing it would make the generation unable to run from a clean clone without that directory, and scoring it would write into another owner's files. The port keeps the algorithms, the row schema and the hash chain, and takes every path from a constructor argument.

independence_evidence.state_root: supplied by the caller; the generation creates control/dispatch, control/events, control/results, artifacts and locators beneath it

fidelity_claim.claim: G1 replicates the transactional factory as of commit dd2fcc63694bea365153a5930472816037b6e4ff. It does NOT claim to replicate the factory as of HEAD, and it is not expected to.
fidelity_claim.why_a_pin_and_not_HEAD: G1 is a generation, and a generation that silently tracks HEAD is not a fixed point anything can be measured against. If the comparison target moved with the live tree, then every later coordinator change to control_plane.py would either move G1's recorded score or turn the fidelity test red without any generation having changed. The G1-to-G2 lift is only a measurement if both endpoints are immutable.
fidelity_claim.chosen_over: re-syncing G1 to the live factory and re-scoring, which was the alternative considered. Re-sync was refused because it would make G1 a moving baseline and would have to be repeated on every subsequent live change, destroying the comparability of the recorded scores.
fidelity_claim.consequence_for_the_reader: Any statement in this cohort's records that G1 'is' the transactional factory means the factory at the pin. A reader comparing G1 against a current checkout of workstreams/po03/tools/control_plane.py should expect differences wherever the live plane has been changed since the pin, and should consult divergence_from_head_after_the_pin below.
fidelity_claim.scores_affected: none. G1's public 21/31 and holdout 7/10 were measured against the packaged port, which has not been edited. No score in workstreams/po03/successor/scores/generation-comparison.json moves as a result of pinning the claim, because pinning changes what is asserted about the port and not the port itself.

divergence_from_head_after_the_pin.surface: repository-relative path normalisation, used by path_in_allowlist and check_ownership
divergence_from_head_after_the_pin.at_the_pin: normalised = path.strip().lstrip('./'), which strips every leading '.' and '/' character rather than a leading './' segment, so '.github/workflows/po03-successor.yml' becomes 'github/workflows/po03-successor.yml' and falls out of the workflow allowlist branch
divergence_from_head_after_the_pin.packaged_in_g1: identical to the pin; G1 carries the same expression verbatim in successor/g1/factory.py
divergence_from_head_after_the_pin.live_behaviour_now: control_plane.normalise_path refuses anything absolute, empty, or containing a '.' or '..' segment, strips only a leading './' segment, and preserves a leading dot in a real name such as '.github'
divergence_from_head_after_the_pin.found_by: workstreams/po03/tests/test_a8_g1_fidelity.py::PathRuleTests, when the cohort branch was merged with the integration branch
divergence_from_head_after_the_pin.reading: G1 is faithful to its pin on this surface: the pre-fix normaliser is what the factory did at dd2fcc6, and `git show dd2fcc6:workstreams/po03/tools/control_plane.py` shows the same lstrip('./') expression. The divergence is between the pin and HEAD, not between G1 and the pin. The fidelity test now compares against the pin, so it measures the port rather than the coordinator's subsequent progress.
divergence_from_head_after_the_pin.does_it_move_a_score: no. Neither the public nor the holdout suite scores a bare-dot workflow path, so no case changes verdict on either side of the divergence. This was checked by re-running score_generations.py --check after the pin was recorded.
divergence_from_head_after_the_pin.note_for_a_future_generation: A G3 packaged after 6f5e386 would carry the corrected normaliser and should record that as a fixed gap relative to G1, pinning its own claim the same way.

post_packaging_edits.edit: docstrings in successor/g1/factory.py were corrected to state fidelity-at-pin instead of fidelity-to-live, and path_in_allowlist gained a comment naming the lstrip('./') behaviour as the pin's behaviour
post_packaging_edits.scope: comments and docstrings only; no statement, expression or control flow was changed
post_packaging_edits.reason: the previous docstring claimed the fidelity test 'loads the live module read-only' and compares against 'the live factory'. That is no longer what the test does and, as the path-rule divergence showed, is not the claim G1 can support. Leaving a false claim inside the generation to preserve a source digest would be the wrong trade.
post_packaging_edits.effect_on_scores: none. generation-comparison.json was regenerated and compared leaf by leaf against the committed document at f15928a: exactly one leaf differs, generations.G1.source_sha256. Every per-case verdict, every suite total (G0 3/31 and 0/10, G1 21/31 and 7/10, G2 31/31 and 10/10), every false-completion count, every guard and the PASS headline at 0.30 holdout lift are byte-identical.
post_packaging_edits.why_the_digest_moved_at_all: the score document records each generation's source digest so a reader can tell which bytes produced a score. A comment-only edit therefore moves the digest without moving the behaviour, which is the correct and honest outcome: the digest tracks the file, and the scores are shown to be unaffected rather than assumed to be.

fidelity_evidence.method: control_plane.py and validate_contracts.py are materialised from git at the pinned commit, verified against the source_sha256 digests above, loaded read-only into a scratch mirror of the tree layout with their writable path constants rebound, and the port is compared against them on ledger row schema, row digest computation, chain verdicts, allowlist and ownership rules, state projection, and real ingest_result admit/reject decisions
fidelity_evidence.comparison_target: the factory at commit dd2fcc63694bea365153a5930472816037b6e4ff, not the working tree
decisions_compared: provider completion without a result commit refused
stale fence after ownership transfer refused
forged fence above the current grant admitted by both

intentional_divergences.divergence: time comes from an injectable clock rather than time.time()
intentional_divergences.reason: a lease-expiry score that depends on wall clock is not reproducible, and reproducibility is a precondition of the comparison
intentional_divergences.scope: affects only when a deadline is judged to have passed; no decision rule changes

intentional_divergences.divergence: admission is adjudicated once, at submit
intentional_divergences.reason: the live factory splits the same checks between make_result.py on the worker side and ingest_result on the parent side. The custody guarantee is identical, because a result that fails any check never enters custody, so the port adjudicates once and the fidelity test compares decisions rather than call sites.
intentional_divergences.scope: check placement only; the set of checks and their grounds are unchanged

gaps_preserved_deliberately.gap: the dispatch record's own manifest digest is never recomputed, so an edit to dispatched immutable input is invisible
cmd_complete writes actor="coordinator" unconditionally, so completion authority is a naming convention rather than an authorisation check
the fence check is incoming < current, so a token that was never granted is accepted for being larger
lease expiry is reported by the recovery scanner but never enforced at commit
artifacts are hashed once at ingestion and never re-verified
duplicate detection matches on the result digest, so a replay under one idempotency key carrying different content is ingested a second time
verify_chain validates links between the rows that remain, so a lost tail leaves a self-consistent chain
RESULT_COMMITTED is terminal for the recovery scanner and there is no outbox, so a committed but uningested result is stranded rather than replayed or re-run
the declared result locator is recorded and never resolved; artifacts are verified against the working tree while result_commit_id is taken on trust
gaps_preserved_deliberately.independently_observed_by: po03-worker-a6 rejected unit a3-u01 because the result record was absent at its declared result_commit_id ee29582dde5c868ac3819a69986c34777d2575ec

fidelity_rule: The port must not be quieter or stronger than what it represents. Every gap above is asserted somewhere: the forged-fence gap is asserted against the live module directly, and the truncation gap is asserted against the live verify_chain. A port that had silently fixed a gap would manufacture lift for G2, so the fidelity tests are part of the measurement, not decoration.
limitations: Fidelity is established on the decision surface the suite scores: row schema, chain verdicts, path rules, projection and ingest decisions. It is not a line-by-line equivalence proof, and behaviour outside that surface, for example the CLI argument handling and the create-from-wave-spec path, is not compared.

The source commit is the wave-A factory branch head that this cohort merged. If the coordinator changes control_plane.py afterwards, this packaging describes the commit named above and not the newer file. That has since happened at least once; see divergence_from_head_after_the_pin.

Fidelity-at-pin is only evaluable in a clone that holds the pinned commit. In a shallow clone the fidelity tests skip with the pin named in the skip reason rather than passing silently. CI checks out with fetch-depth: 0, so the pin resolves there.
